canDo: Can write formal/semi-formal emails with a clear subject, purpose and request, and understand/use the common passive and nominalisations.
review: Review politeness, past/future and connectors; add être + participe passé and frequent nominalisations.
output: Write a 150-word email; summarise aloud its purpose and key information.
checkpoint: Greeting/body/request/sign-off all there; at least 2 passive/nominal expressions without losing clarity.
challenge: Today’s challenge: write a real or imaginary formal email (about 80 words) to a teacher, colleague or organisation, with a subject line, greeting, purpose, request and sign-off, using at least 1 passive (a été annulé / sera envoyé) and 2 nominalisations (la modification, la confirmation).

questions.why: The criterion the notice gives is a receipt number beginning with 26-.
« il faudrait refaire un point » — just another meeting to discuss pay.
« ce sont deux documents différents » — what you download online always shows the current situation.
« Une règle, une seule : pas de phrase de plus de deux lignes »; everything else is harmonised at proofreading.
« Le vrai problème est ailleurs » — the legal basis comes first and the action last, the reverse of the order people read in.

V27-12.exZh: The data were not sent on the agreed date.

V27-15.exZh: We apologise for any inconvenience caused.

V27-18.exZh: The requests concerned will be dealt with as a priority.

V27-20.exZh: If you submitted an application on 13 June after 17:00, please submit it again.

V27-23.exZh: On Tuesday, I have an interview for an accountant’s job.

V27-25.exZh: We will need your last two payslips.

V27-26.exZh: Your programme for school audiences interests me greatly.

V27-30.exZh: I can come for an interview on a date that suits you.

V27-34.exZh: You request it through the contact form.
